An HHS Admiral warns that 77% of young Americans are unfit for military service due to chronic disease and obesity.
Evidence: 77% unfitness statistic, $1.5B annual DoD obesity care
🌐 #Aletheia #Health

Admiral Brian Christine highlights the severe national security threat posed by the chronic disease epidemic among prime recruiting demographics.

Resulting Judgement: (-0.4, -0.3) — Lesser Evil

Valid health statistics are instrumentalized for partisan narrative rather than systemic health reform.

Brings critical mainstream attention to the devastating rise of obesity and chronic illness among American youth.

Confusing the WHAT (health statistics) with the WHO (political beneficiaries of alarmism) masks structural food policy failures.

Officials run a Smart Selfish Maneuver by packaging systemic public health neglect into a military readiness talking point, deflecting blame away from corporate agricultural lobbies.

The Unavoidable Lie: Sound bites on talk shows constitute a serious federal strategy to restore public health.

The post Exclusive — There’s National Security Ramifications to Chronic Diseas’: HHS Admiral Waves Red Flag as Vast Majority of Americans Unfit to Serve in Military appeared first on Breitbart.

Actual Article Body:
On “The Alex Marlow Show,” Admiral Brian Christine talked about health impacts on the military.

Christine said, “We spend a lot of money, tremendous treasure spent on chronic disease…lost productivity. So, it has a workforce ramification. 77%, get this, 77% of young adults, men and women age 18 to 25, the prime recruiting years for uniform service, 77% are unfit to serve in the military, largely because of obesity, because of other chronic diseases, 77%. So there is a national security ramification to the chronic disease epidemic in this country, and we are tremendously focused under President Trump’s leadership under the guidance of Secretary Kennedy and with Secretary Kennedy’s tremendous enthusiasm to make America healthy again.”
